title: Abstract
excerpt: Vitamin D insufficiency and secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) are associated with increased morbidity and mortality in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and are poorly addressed by current treatments.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Two identical multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies enrolled subjects from 89 US sites.

title: Methods
excerpt: A total of 213 subjects were randomized in study A (72 received placebo and 141 received ER calcifediol), and 216 subjects were randomized in study B (72 received placebo and 144 received ER calcifediol).

title: Abstract
excerpt: ER calcifediol normalized serum total 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations (>30 ng/ml) in >95% of per-protocol subjects and reduced plasma intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH) by at least 10% in 72%.

title: Abstract
excerpt: The proportion of subjects receiving ER calcifediol who achieved iPTH reductions of ≥30% increased progressively with treatment duration, reaching 22, 40 and 50% at 12, 26 and 52 weeks, respectively.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Conclusion: Oral ER calcifediol is safe and effective in treating SHPT and vitamin D insufficiency in CKD.

title: Introduction
excerpt: SHPT affects 40 and 82% of patients with stages 3 and 4 CKD [3], respectively, and requires prompt and effective treatment.

title: Introduction
excerpt: Vitamin D insufficiency affects an estimated 71–83% of patients with stage 3 or 4 CKD [5, 6].

title: Introduction
excerpt: It is defined in clinical practice guidelines applicable to CKD as serum total 25-hydroxyvitamin D <30 ng/ml [7, 8]

title: Methods
excerpt: Subjects were stratified equally by CKD stage and were randomized in a 2: 1 ratio to receive a once daily 30 μg oral dose of ER calcifediol (or matching placebo) for 12 weeks at bedtime followed by an additional 14 weeks of treatment with once daily bedtime doses of either 30 or 60 μg of ER calcifediol (or placebo).

title: Methods
excerpt: The dose was increased to 60 μg at the start of week 13 if plasma iPTH remained >70 pg/ml (the upper limit of the laboratory reference range), serum total 25-hydroxyvitamin D was <65 ng/ml and serum Ca was <9.8 mg/dl.

title: Methods
excerpt: The sole primary efficacy end point in all 3 studies was the number (n, %) of subjects in the intent-to-treat (ITT) population that attained a mean decrease of ≥30% in plasma iPTH from pretreatment baseline in the efficacy assessment period (EAP), defined as the last 6 weeks of the 26- and 52-week treatment periods.

title: Methods
excerpt: A total of 354 subjects (83%) completed studies A or B, and 298 (69%) entered a single 6-month open-label extension study during which dosing continued unchanged

title: Methods
excerpt: Eligible subjects were ≥18 years of age and had CKD (not requiring regular dialysis) with eGFR ≥15 and <60 ml/min/1.73 m2.

title: Methods
excerpt: Other eligibility criteria included serum total 25-hydroxyvitamin D ≥10 and <30 ng/ml, plasma iPTH ≥85 and <500 pg/ml, serum Ca ≥8.4 and <9.8 mg/dl and serum P ≥2.0 and <5.0 mg/dl.

title: Methods
excerpt: Exclusion criteria included a spot urine Ca:Cr ratio >0.2, nephrotic range proteinuria (>3 mg/mg Cr) and history of parathyroidectomy for SHPT or renal transplantation.

title: Results
excerpt: The subjects’ mean age was 66 years (range 25–85), 50% were male, 65% White, 32% African-American or Black, 21% Hispanic and 3% Other.

title: Results
excerpt: At baseline, subjects had SHPT and stage 3 (52%) or stage 4 (48%) CKD.

title: Methods
excerpt: Plasma iPTH and serum Ca, phosphorus (P) and total 25-hydroxyvitamin D were measured every 2 or 4 weeks in studies A and B and in the subsequent extension.

title: Results
excerpt: In the ITT population, the proportion of subjects who achieved at least a 30% reduction in plasma iPTH in the EAP was greater with ER calcifediol than with placebo treatment in both studies (33 vs. 8% in study A (p < 0.001) and 34 vs. 7% in study B (p < 0.001)) irrespective of whether the CKD stages were combined or analyzed separately.

title: Results
excerpt: Six subjects (2%) in the ER calcifediol treatment group and no subjects (0%) in the placebo group required dose reductions for protocol-defined hypercalcemia (2 consecutive serum Ca values >10.3 mg/dl).

title: Results
excerpt: The percentages of subjects that experienced at least one TEAE were comparable in the pooled placebo (69.4%) and ER calcifediol (67.4%) groups.

title: Discussion
excerpt: Patients with massive proteinuria were excluded from participation in these 2 studies. It is, therefore, unknown if ER calcifediol therapy could overcome proteinuric loss of 25-hydroxyvitamin D in these patients.

title: Discussion
excerpt: No data from these studies have suggested that ER calcifediol has an adverse effect on renal function; mean serum Cr increase and mean eGFR decline were similar in the active and placebo groups.

title: Conclusions
excerpt: These data presented from the two 26-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials and a subsequent 26-week extension study show that oral ER calcifediol administered in daily bedtime doses of 30 or 60 μg is safe and effective in treating SHPT and correcting the underlying vitamin D insufficiency in adult patients with stage 3 or 4 CKD.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Vitamin D insufficiency drives secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) and is associated with increased cardiovascular mortality in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD).

title: Abstract
excerpt: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated MR calcifediol in CKD subjects (n = 78) with plasma intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH) >70 pg/ml and serum total 25-hydroxyvitamin D <30 ng/ml.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Subjects received daily treatment for six weeks with oral MR calcifediol (30, 60 or 90 μg) or a placebo.

title: Results
excerpt: The 6-week course of daily MR calcifediol effectively treated vitamin D insufficiency as more than 90% of subjects in the 30, 60 and 90 μg dose groups achieved adequate serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels (≥30 ng/ml) by EOT compared with only 3% in the pooled placebo group (p < 0.0001).

title: Abstract
excerpt: Mean plasma iPTH decreased from baseline (140.3 pg/ml) by 20.9 ± 6.2% (SE), 32.8 ± 5.7 and 39.3 ± 4.3% in the 30, 60 and 90 μg dose groups, respectively, and increased 17.2 ± 7.8% in the pooled placebo group (p < 0.005).

title: Abstract
excerpt: Conclusion: Oral MR calcifediol appears safe and highly effective in treating SHPT associated with vitamin D insufficiency in CKD.

title: Methods
excerpt: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involved 78 subjects recruited from 16 US sites into two cohorts studied sequentially. Subjects in each cohort were randomized to 6 weeks of daily treatment with either MR calcifediol or a matching placebo, followed by 6 weeks of post-treatment monitoring.

title: Methods
excerpt: In Cohort 1, a total of 51 subjects were assigned to three treatment groups (n = 17) receiving MR calcifediol (60 or 90 μg) or placebo.

title: Methods
excerpt: In Cohort 2, 27 subjects were assigned to two treatment groups receiving 30 μg of MR calcifediol (n = 13) or placebo (n = 14).

title: Methods
excerpt: Eligible subjects had ages between 18 and 85 (inclusive) and CKD (not requiring regular dialysis) as evidenced by an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of ≥25 and <70 ml/min/1.73 m2.

title: Methods
excerpt: The primary efficacy endpoints were the proportion of subjects that achieved (a) serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels of ≥30 ng/ml and (b) mean percent reductions of plasma iPTH of ≥30% from pre-treatment baseline at the end of treatment (EOT).

title: Introduction
excerpt: Consensus is lacking on the definition of vitamin D insufficiency with K/DOQI, for example, defining it as <30 ng/ml and the Institute of Medicine (IOM) favoring <20 ng/ml

title: Introduction
excerpt: The present study evaluated a modified-release (MR) formulation of calcifediol, designed to raise serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D in a gradual manner to physiological levels (≥30 to ≤100 ng/ml), avoiding excessive induction of CYP24.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Introduction: Obesity increases the risk of vitamin D insufficiency, which exacerbates secondary hyperparathyroidism in chronic kidney disease.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Recent studies suggest that serum total 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25OHD) levels of ≥50 ng/mL are necessary to produce significant reductions in elevated parathyroid hormone levels in nondialysis patients.

title: Abstract
excerpt: More than 50% of subjects treated with vitamin D supplements in both real-world studies (Studies 1 and 2) failed to achieve serum 25OHD levels ≥30 ng/mL, a level widely viewed by nephrologists as the threshold of adequacy; only 7.3–7.5% of subjects achieved levels ≥50 ng/mL.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Data from the European study (Study 1) showed that serum 25OHD levels had significant and nearly identical inverse relationships with BW and BMI, indicating that high BW or BMI thwarts the ability of vitamin D supplements to raise serum 25OHD.

title: Abstract
excerpt: One RCT (Study 3) showed that 8 weeks of ERC treatment (60 μg/day) raised serum 25OHD levels to ≥30 and 50 ng/mL in all subjects, regardless of BW, while cholecalciferol (300,000 IU/month) raised serum 25OHD to these thresholds in 56% and 0% of subjects, respectively.

title: Abstract
excerpt: The other RCT (Study 4) showed that ERC treatment (30 or 60 μg/day) successfully raised mean serum 25OHD levels to at least 50 ng/mL for subjects in all BW categories, whereas no increases were observed with placebo treatment.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Conclusion: Real-world studies conducted in Europe and USA in nondialysis patients (Studies 1 and 2) showed that vitamin D supplements (cholecalciferol or ergocalciferol) were unreliable in raising serum total 25OHD to targets of 30 or 50 ng/mL.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Medical records of 376 adult patients with stage 3–4 CKD and a history of SHPT and VDI from 15 United States (US) nephrology clinics were reviewed for up to 1 year pre- and post-ERC, NVD or AVD initiation.

title: Abstract
excerpt: The mean age of the study population was 69.5 years, with gender and racial distributions representative of the US CKD population.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Enrolled patients were grouped by treatment into three cohorts: ERC (n = 174), AVD (n = 55) and NVD (n = 147), and mean baseline levels were similar for serum 25D (18.8–23.5 ng/mL), calcium (Ca: 9.1–9.3 mg/dL), phosphorus (P: 3.7–3.8 mg/dL) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR: 30.3–35.7 mL/min/1.73m2).

title: Abstract
excerpt: Serum 25D rose in all cohorts (p < 0.001) during treatment. ERC yielded the highest increase (p < 0.001) of 23.7 ± 1.6 ng/mL versus 9.7 ± 1.5 and 5.5 ± 1.3 ng/mL for NVD and AVD, respectively.

title: Abstract
excerpt: PTH declined with ERC treatment by 34.1 ± 6.6 pg/mL (p < 0.001) but remained unchanged in the other two cohorts.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Conclusions: Real-world clinical effectiveness and safety varied across the therapies under investigation, but only ERC effectively raised mean 25D (to well above 30 ng/mL) and reduced mean PTH levels without causing hypercalcemia.

title: Limitations
excerpt: This study was not powered or of sufficient duration to examine endpoints related to cardiovascular disease, fractures, hospitalization rates and mortality.

title: Limitations
excerpt: The nature of the study design, as with any retrospective chart review, led to certain limitations: medical records may have been incomplete, due to missing data points, or involvement of multiple sites

title: Limitations
excerpt: Selection bias towards a more severe population may have been introduced by the inclusion criterion ensuring patients had documentation of serum 25D and PTH levels before and after the index date.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Vitamin D deficiency (serum total 25-OH vitamin D levels < 30 ng/mL) occurs early in the course of chronic kidney disease and treatment guidelines recommend early intervention to restore 25-OH vitamin D levels as a first step to prevent/delay the onset/progression of secondary hyperparathyroidism.

title: Abstract
excerpt: The vitamin D forms administered to replace 25-OH vitamin D include cholecalciferol, ergocalciferol, and immediate- or extended-release formulations of calcifediol.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Extended-release calcifediol increases circulating 25-OH vitamin D levels in a dose-dependent manner and lowers parathyroid hormone levels by a clinically relevant extent, comparable to what can be achieved by administering active vitamin D analogues, though with a lower risk of hypercalcaemia and hyperphosphataemia.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Active vitamin D analogues are reserved for patients undergoing dialysis or pre-dialysis patients with severe progressive secondary hyperparathyroidism.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Most patients with intermediate-stage chronic kidney disease will develop secondary hyperparathyroidism before dialysis is required.

title: Editorial
excerpt: What are the ideal concentrations of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25D) needed to maintain adequate amounts of active 1,25D-dihydroxyvitamin D (1,25D) and prevent maladaptive secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) in patients with stage 3-4 chronic kidney disease (CKD)?

title: Editorial
excerpt: The KDIGO group acknowledged that optimal concentrations of PTH in non-dialyzed CKD patients were not precisely known.

title: Editorial
excerpt: Although the results in the current trial represent an enticing look into the effectiveness of a potential new tool for treatment of SHPT in CKD patients, the authors acknowledge that it remains unknown whether complete normalization of PTH is an appropriate goal for vitamin D repletion.

title: Editorial
excerpt: Their study criteria included a precisely defined subset of CKD patients with no apparent deficits in calcium homeostasis, and as such, the safety of this treatment protocol cannot yet be generalized to include patients who do not fit this specific profile.

title: Editorial
excerpt: Their study size was also relatively modest and limited to 26 weeks of intervention.

title: Editorial
excerpt: Nevertheless, these positive findings would lead us to conclude that larger and longer studies are worthy to pursue to further explore the safety and effectiveness of this potential new therapy for SHPT in CKD patients.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Vitamin D insufficiency is prevalent in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and associated with secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) and increased risk of bone and vascular disease.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Unfortunately, supplementation of stage 3 or 4 CKD patients with currently recommended vitamin D2 or D3 regimens does not reliably restore serum total 25-hydroxyvitamin D to adequacy

title: Abstract
excerpt: Bolus IV calcifediol produced rapid increases in serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D3, calcitriol and FGF23, along with significant induction of CYP24A1 in both kidney and parathyroid gland.

title: Abstract
excerpt: In contrast, oral MR calcifediol produced gradual increases in serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 and calcitriol and achieved similar hormonal exposure, yet neither CYP24A1 nor FGF23 were induced.

title: Abstract
excerpt: A 10-fold greater exposure to bolus IV than oral MR calcifediol was required to similarly lower intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH).

title: Abstract
excerpt: Taken together, these studies indicate that rapid increases in 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 trigger CYP24A1 and FGF23 induction, limiting effective exposure to calcitriol and iPTH reduction in SHPT. They also support further investigation of gradual vitamin D repletion for improved clinical effectiveness.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Introduction: Extended-release calcifediol (ERC) is an orally administered prohormone of active vitamin D (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D [1,25D]) designed to safely and sufficiently increase serum total 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25D) to reduce elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH) in patients with nondialysis-chronic kidney disease (ND-CKD).

title: Abstract
excerpt: ERC is currently approved in the United States and Canada.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Currently available treatment options for secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) in NDCKD have limitations: the effectiveness of nutritional vitamin D supplements for reduction of PTH levels is unproven and active (1α-hydroxylated) vitamin D analogues elevate serum calcium, which increases the risk of hypercalcemia and vascular calcification.

title: Abstract
excerpt: Clinical studies show that ERC is an effective, well tolerated treatment for SHPT in ND-CKD.

title: 10 用药过量
excerpt: RAYALDEE用药过量可导致高钙尿、高钙血症、高磷酸血症或iPTH过度抑制。维生素D用药过量的常见症状可能包括便秘、食欲减退、脱水、疲乏、易激惹、肌肉无力或呕吐。

title: 10 用药过量
excerpt: 对RAYALDEE急性意外用药过量的治疗方法应包括一般支持疗法。如果在短时间内发现用药过量，则诱导呕吐或进行洗胃，防止进一步吸收。连续测定血清钙和尿钙水平，并评估高钙血症引起的任何心电图异常。停止补充钙。如果血清钙水平持续明显升高，则使用标准医疗护理进行治疗。

title: 7.1 CYP3A抑制剂
excerpt: 细胞色素P450抑制剂，如酮康唑、阿扎那韦、克拉霉素、茚地那韦、伊曲康唑、奈法唑酮、奈非那韦、利托那韦、沙奎那韦、泰利霉素或伏立康唑，可抑制参与维生素D代谢的酶（CYP24A1和CYP27B1），还可能改变血清骨化二醇水平。如果患者开始或中止强效CYP3A4抑制剂治疗，可能需调整RAYALDEE剂量，应密切监测血清25-羟基维生素D、iPTH、血清钙浓度。

title: 7.2 噻嗪类
excerpt: 噻嗪类与RAYALDEE合并使用可能导致高钙血症。在这种情况下，可能需要更为频繁地监测患者的血清钙水平[请见警告与注意事项（5.1）]。

title: 7.3 考来烯胺
excerpt: 据报道，考来烯胺可减弱肠道对脂溶性维生素的吸收，因此可能影响对骨化二醇（RAYALDEE的活性成分）的吸收。如果患者开始或中止考来烯胺治疗，可能需调整RAYALDEE剂量，并密切监测血清总25-羟基维生素D、iPTH、血清钙浓度。

title: 7.4 其他药物
excerpt: 苯巴比妥或其他抗惊厥药或其他刺激微粒体羟基化的化合物可缩短RAYALDEE活性成分骨化二醇的半衰期。如果患者开始或中止苯巴比妥或其他抗惊厥药治疗，可能需调整RAYALDEE剂量，并密切监测血清总25-羟基维生素D、iPTH、血清钙浓度。

title: 12.1 作用机制
excerpt: 骨化二醇（25-羟基维生素D3）是维生素D3活性形式-骨化三醇（1,25-二羟维生素D3）的激素原。

title: 12.1 作用机制
excerpt: 骨化二醇通过细胞色素P450 27B1（CYP27B1）（还称为1-α羟化酶，主要在肾脏中）转化为骨化三醇。

title: 第七章 骨质疏松性骨折 / 三、老年人补充骨化二醇对肌肉功能的影响
excerpt:
2021年Gonnelli等[10]评估50例骨量减少/骨质疏松症女性患者（血清25(OH)D水平在10- 20 ng/ml之间）每日补充两种不同剂量骨化二醇的疗效和安全性，随机分为两组，分别口 服骨化二醇每日20 μg（25例）或30 μg（25例），共6个月。结果：①20 μg组患者治疗90 天后25(OH)D水平达到峰值（59.3 ng/ml），30 μg组患者仅治疗60天后25(OH)D水平达到 峰值（72.3 ng/ml）。②两组患者的25(OH)D水平均趋于稳定。③30天后，所有接受30 μg/ 天治疗的患者25(OH)D水平均>30 ng/ml。④握力能持续略有增加，在30 μg组中达到具有 统计学意义的增加。⑤30 μg组患者的血清肌肉生长抑制素水平也略有下降，但无统计学意 义。结论：骨化二醇能够快速纠正维生素D缺乏症，建议需要快速达到最佳25(OH)D水平的
骨量减少/骨质疏松症患者每日服⽤30 μg。此外，使⽤30 μg/天剂量的骨化二醇进行6个月 的治疗，可使上肢力量出现适度但显著的增加。

title: 第七章 骨质疏松性骨折 / 三、老年人补充骨化二醇对肌肉功能的影响
excerpt: 2012年Bischoff-Ferrari等[11]评估20名健康绝经后妇女（61.5±7.2岁，25(OH)D水平为 13.2±3.9 ng/mL）补充25(OH)D3（骨化二醇）与维生素D3，观察对血清25(OH)D水平、下 肢功能、血压和先天免疫标志物影响的随机双盲临床研究。分别每日服⽤20 μg骨化二醇或 20 μg(800 IU)维生素D3。共4个月。结果：①骨化二醇组的平均25(OH)D水平升高至69.5 ng/mL。这种升高是即时的，并且持续存在；而维生素D3组平均25(OH)D水平升高至31.0 ng/mL，其升高速度较慢。②与维生素D3组相比，骨化二醇组女性下肢功能维持或改善的 几率提高了2.8倍（比值比[OR]=2.79；95%CI，1.18–6.58），收缩压降低了5.7 mmHg （p=0.0002）。
